οὐ,  the negative of fact and statement, as μή of will and thought; οὐ denies, μή rejects; οὐ is absolute, μή relative;
οὕτως,  and before a consonant οὕτω (but sometimes οὕτως before a consonant, Refs 5th c.BC+, and οὕτω before a vowel is
Included with:  οὐ,  the negative of fact and statement, as μή of will and thought; οὐ denies, μή rejects; οὐ is absolut

παρ-άγω,  future παράξω Refs 5th c.BC+: perfect παραγέωχα Refs 2nd c.BC+:—lead by or past a place, with accusative loci,
παρατίθημι,  Doric dialect and poetry παρτίθημι (late forms from παρατίθω Refs; 3rd.pers. singular παρτιθεῖ, παρατιθεῖ,
παρουσ-ία, ἡ,  (πάρειμι) presence, of persons, δεσπότου, etc., Refs 4th c.BC+; ἀνδρῶν π., ={ἄνδρες οἱ παρόντες}, Refs 5t
πέρᾱν,  Ionic dialect and Epic dialect πέρην, adverb on the other side, across, in early Poets always with genitive, esp
